episode.title: Cariboo Signals - Cariboo Local Affairs
episode.description:
Riley and Casey explore technology and society in rural communities. Today's focus: Cariboo Local Affairs.

THIS WEEK WE'RE ASKING: Does a place still exist if nobody records it?

NEWS ROUNDUP: We break down UBCM backs Williams Lake call for increased dead wood salvage, expedited permitting and Williams Lake Stampeders out of 2026-27 CIHL season giving heartfelt thanks to fans, plus 10 more stories, and explore what these developments mean for communities like ours.

RURAL CONNECTIONS: Is BC's overlapping provincial and municipal election calendar creating an accountability gap by reducing local media coverage of certain races? Topics include: Williams Lake mayoral rematch between Surinderpal Rathor and Walt Cobb, including Cobb's 2021 residential school misinformation controversy, Williams Lake council race with 14 candidates, three with partial records and eleven with no public information, CRD electoral area director races (Areas D, E, F) with no publicly accessible candidate lists despite filed nominations, School District 27 trustee races, specifically Zone 6's unopposed incumbent Michael Franklin, Local media capacity constraints and the role of overlapping provincial elections in reducing coverage of municipal races.

Hosts: Riley (Tech optimist with an engineering background) and Casey (Community-first skeptic of tech promises).

COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHT: CMHA South Cariboo

discussion.central_question: Is BC's overlapping provincial and municipal election calendar creating an accountability gap by reducing local media coverage of certain races?
discussion.riley_position: The overlapping elections create real, fixable gaps in coverage—particularly for lower-profile races like CRD director seats—where candidates and records simply aren't being documented or made public before voters cast ballots.
riley_key_evidence: Eleven of fourteen Williams Lake council candidates have no findable prior record, biography, or public information beyond their nomination forms
CRD Areas D, E, and F have no publicly filed candidate list available despite nominations closing September 11th
School trustee Zone 6 has only one unopposed candidate (Michael Franklin) running by acclamation with no contested record to review
discussion.casey_position: The media capacity problem is real but uneven—high-profile races like the mayoral rematch will get coverage regardless, while quieter seats get ignored not because information doesn't exist but because it hasn't been made accessible to the public or treated as newsworthy by outlets.
casey_key_evidence: Williams Lake Mayor Walt Cobb shared misinformation about residential schools in late 2021 while in office and was called to resign by Williams Lake First Nation, creating a documented record for voters to consider
CRD's own website lists current directors Steve Forseth (Area D) and Melynda Neufeld (Area E) but couldn't confirm Area F's current director at all
Candidate information exists on paper in returning officer files but hasn't been published in places residents would find it without already knowing to call the CRD directly
discussion.resolution: The hosts agreed the gap is fixable rather than systemic—they called on the Regional District to publish its filed candidate lists on cariboord.ca and asked local outlets to pursue quiet races even without dramatic hooks, while inviting listeners to send candidate information before the October 17th vote.
